cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! It's so good to see you again.

cues.caption: Last time: work backwards · 9 + 3 = 12
cues.text: Last time, we worked backwards. Mina had nine stickers after losing three. So we added the three back, and found she started with twelve.

cues.caption: Chapter 4 · Breaking Big Problems Into Small Ones
cues.text: Today is chapter four of Problem Solver. It's called, Breaking Big Problems Into Small Ones.

cues.caption: Ever felt a job was way too big?
cues.text: Have you ever looked at a job and thought, whoa, that's way too big? Hmm. Today, I'll show you a trick that makes big jobs feel small.

cues.caption: "Riya, please clean your room!"
cues.text: Meet Riya. It's Sunday morning, and Mum calls out, Riya, Nani is coming this evening. Please clean your room!

cues.caption: Toys, books, a messy bed… Oh no!
cues.text: Riya looks around. Toys on the floor. Books everywhere. And the bed is one big, crumpled mess. Oh no!

cues.caption: Where do I even start? What would you do?
cues.text: Riya just stands there. Where do I even start? It all feels too big. What would you do, if you were Riya? Think for a moment.

cues.caption: Toys · Books · Bed: three small jobs
cues.text: Here's a smart idea. Don't clean the whole room at once. Split it into small jobs. Pick up the toys. Put the books on the shelf. Make the bed.

cues.caption: One small job at a time → clean room!
cues.text: Now Riya does one small job at a time. Toys, done. Books, done. Bed, done. And look! The whole room is clean, and it didn't even feel hard.

cues.caption: That trick is called DECOMPOSITION
cues.text: What Riya did has a special name. It's called decomposition.

cues.caption: Breaking a big problem into small parts
cues.text: De, com, po, si, tion. A long word, but the meaning is simple. Decomposition means breaking a big problem into smaller, easier parts.

cues.caption: A roti: one small bite at a time
cues.text: Think about eating a roti. You can't stuff the whole roti in your mouth at once! You tear it into small pieces, and eat one bite at a time. Yum.

cues.caption: Small task = one job you can finish
cues.text: Each piece is a small task. A small task is one simple job that you can finish on its own.

cues.caption: Big job: pack the school bag
cues.text: That night, Riya has another big job. Packing her school bag for Monday.

cues.caption: Books · Bottle · Lunch box · Pencil box
cues.text: What small jobs are hiding inside it? Her books, her water bottle, her lunch box, and her pencil box.

cues.caption: Timetable → Books → Bottle → Lunch box
cues.text: Now let's put them in order. One, check today's timetable. Two, put in those books. Three, fill the water bottle. Four, add the lunch box.

cues.caption: Then decide: first, next, last
cues.text: Why check the timetable first? Because it tells you which books you need! So after you break a job, you also decide the order. What comes first, next, and last.

cues.caption: Nani is here! Riya makes nimbu pani
cues.text: Let's go back to the evening. Nani arrives, and it's so hot! Riya decides to make her some nimbu pani.

cues.caption: Squeeze → Water → Sugar → Pour & serve
cues.text: First, squeeze the lemons. Then, add water. Next, stir in some sugar. And last, pour it into a glass, and serve.

cues.caption: Serve first? Nothing to pour! Serve LAST
cues.text: Could Riya pour and serve it first? No way! There's nothing to pour yet. Serving comes last, because you can only serve it after it's made.

cues.caption: Nani's puzzle: what is 23 + 45?
cues.text: Nani loves maths puzzles. She asks Riya, what is twenty three plus forty five?

cues.caption: 23 = 20 + 3 · 45 = 40 + 5
cues.text: Riya breaks each number into tens and ones. Twenty three is twenty and three. Forty five is forty and five.

cues.caption: Tens: 20 + 40 = 60 · Ones: 3 + 5 = 8
cues.text: Add the tens. Twenty plus forty equals sixty. Now add the ones. Three plus five equals eight.
Put them together. Sixty and eight make sixty eight! Two small sums were easier than one big one.

cues.caption: What is 6 × 14?
cues.text: Nani smiles, and asks a trickier one. What is six times fourteen? Hmm. That's a big one to do in your head.

cues.caption: Break it up: 14 = 10 + 4
cues.text: So let's break fourteen into ten and four. Look at the dots. Six rows of ten, and six rows of four.

cues.caption: 6 × 10 = 60 · 6 × 4 = 24
cues.text: Six times ten is sixty. And six times four is twenty four.

cues.caption: 60 + 24 = 84. So 6 × 14 = 84!
cues.text: Now add them up. Sixty plus twenty four equals eighty four. So, six times fourteen is eighty four!

cues.caption: Coders use decomposition every day!
cues.text: Riya's cousin Arjun is a coder. He makes games! And guess what? He uses decomposition every single day.

cues.caption: Pitch · Bat · Ball · Score
cues.text: Arjun wants to make a cricket game. That's huge! So he breaks it into parts. Draw the pitch. Make the bat swing. Move the ball. Keep the score.

cues.caption: Algorithms are built in small parts too
cues.text: Each part gets its own step by step plan. And a step by step plan to solve a problem is called an algorithm. Big programs are built from small, clear parts, in the right order.

cues.caption: Which is NOT part of cleaning a room?
cues.text: Game time! Remember Riya's room? Which of these is NOT a small part of cleaning a room? Pick up toys. Make the bed. Fly a kite. Put books on the shelf. Think!

cues.caption: Fly a kite doesn't help clean the room!
cues.text: Fly a kite! It's lots of fun, but it doesn't help clean the room at all. Every small part should help finish the big job.

cues.caption: Party steps are mixed up! What's the order?
cues.text: One more! Riya's class is having a party. Here are the steps, all mixed up. Buy snacks. Set up, and enjoy. Pick a date. Make a guest list. What's the best order? Pause, and think.

cues.caption: Date → Guest list → Snacks → Set up & enjoy
cues.text: First, pick a date. Then, make a guest list, so you know who's coming. Next, buy snacks. And last, set up, and enjoy! Plan first, then shop, then party.

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, your turn. Here's a practice check, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Break 'make a birthday card' into 4 steps
cues.text: Tomorrow is Nani's birthday, and Riya wants to make her a card. Break, make a birthday card, into four small steps, in order. Pause the video, and try it on paper.

cues.caption: Fold → Draw → Write → Sign & give
cues.text: Here's one way. One, fold the paper. Two, draw a picture on the front. Three, write a message inside. Four, sign your name, and give it. Folding comes first, because you need a card before you can draw on it! Brilliant!

cues.caption: Big job → small jobs
cues.text: Let's remember what we learned. Decomposition means breaking a big job into small jobs.

cues.caption: Put the small jobs in order
cues.text: Then, put the small jobs in order.

cues.caption: Do one small job at a time
cues.text: Do one small job at a time, just like eating a roti, bite by bite.

cues.caption: Algorithms & sums are built in parts
cues.text: And algorithms, and even big sums, are built in parts too.

cues.caption: Chapter 4 done!
cues.text: Chapter four, done! You can break big jobs into small steps, just like Riya. Super work, champ!

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
